description: GET /api/v1/miners — rank catalog ASICs by daily profit for a home or small-business solar+battery+grid setup (same model as the site calculator). Optional solarW (10000=10 kW), batteryCapacity (kWh), zipCode, elecCost, and powerSources override the API-key owner profile. Example: 10 kW array + 20 kWh battery → solarW=10000, batteryCapacity=20, powerSources={solar:true, battery:true, grid:true}; sort PROFIT/DAY. Includes Kadena/KDA, NexaPow/NEXA, XPHash/XP, SHA-256 QUAI, and NiceHash daily revenue when a rate exists. Figures are MinerYield model estimates from live market inputs: estimates only, not investment, financial, or tax advice, and not ROI guarantees. Results vary with network difficulty, coin price, power cost, and hardware performance. Do your own research.

batteryCapacity.description: Battery storage in kWh (20 = 20 kWh). Only used when powerSources.battery is true (passing batteryCapacity without powerSources turns battery on). Excess daytime solar charges the battery; the battery covers night hours before grid.

elecCost.description: Grid electricity price in USD per kWh (0.15 = 15 cents). Applied only to leftover watts after solar and battery. There is no separate day/night rate: solar covers the sun window, grid covers the rest at this price. On list_miners this overrides the API-key owner profile.

powerSources.description: Which legs of the site calculator to use. solar=true uses solarW during Peak Sun Hours; battery=true uses leftover solar stored in batteryCapacity at night; grid=true keeps the miner running 24h on leftover grid kWh. solar=true + grid=true + battery=false is "solar by day, grid at night". If grid=false the miner only runs while solar or battery energy lasts (runtimeHours < 24).

battery.description: Use leftover daytime solar stored in batteryCapacity to cover night hours.

grid.description: Draw leftover kWh from the grid at elecCost so the miner can run 24 hours. Off = solar/battery-only runtime.

solar.description: Use the solar array (solarW) during Peak Sun Hours. Turn on for any home-solar scenario.

solarW.description: Home/small-business solar array capacity in Watts (10000 = 10 kW). Used with Peak Sun Hours from zipCode. Solar generation is treated as free during the sun window; leftover watts can charge the battery.

zipCode.description: 5-digit US ZIP for Peak Sun Hours. Defaults to the API-key owner profile, then a server default. Needed for a realistic solar-by-day estimate.
